title: I Posted the Community-Greenhouse Mister Hours After They Camped the Bench

parts.text: I walked the tomato aisle at 7:08 a.m. and chair Pilar was already sitting under our numbered mister. The clipboard said: ONE BENCH. FORTY MINUTES. MISTER FOLLOWS THE BOOKING. I was forty-four, greenhouse volunteer, holding a watering card that listed our bay. Pilar shrugged. "Chairs are climate." I photographed the clipboard, the booking, and her crate on our slats. Then I asked for the mister log. At 7:16 horticulture pinged why Pilar's name was on our cycle. I kept my voice humid-soft and let the timestamp talk. A clipboard is only a clipboard until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Horticulture can see Pilar's crate on our bench during our cycle.

social.video_title: She camped our numbered mister on our bench — Part 1/2
social.description: Greenhouse aisle, a chair on our slats, a forty-minute clock she posted. I logged the mist. Would you have asked for the mister log?

parts.text: Pilar called it a check until horticulture asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the clipboard, and the crate still. The mister went back to our bay. Pilar ran her own forty and told the next chair atmosphere was always about humidity. Humidity is a word chairs use when a booking exists. Bench policy now has a second line: CHAIRS ARE NOT CLIMATE. I keep our card on a labeled clip. Pilar brown-bags her jokes. The aisle finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Mister log, numbered bench, and a second line on the clipboard. Was a check ever our slats?
